newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Sept 26.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Manly will prove too much of a powerhouse for the unconditioned Dragons according to Canterbury's Terry Lamb, who captained the Bulldogs' unexpected win over the Sea Eagles in last season's rugby league grand final. Page 36.

ARU chairman Ken Arthurson has backed away from moves to rationalise clubs in Sydney, saying it would tear the heart out of the game. Although previously promoting the reduction of Sydney clubs for the national expansion of the game, Arthurson now claims it wll do more harm than good. Page 34.

The owner of Gossips will be asked to a stewards inquiry at Randwick on Monday where he will be invited to give his reasons for the gelding's sudden stable transfer, following the controversial Shannon Quality at Rosehill on Saturday. Page 35.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Adam Ritson is still in critical condition as doctors fight to save his life, as reports indicate his health is less stable than thought. Still in intensive care, the Parramatta prop forward's mother has maintained a 15-hour-a-day vigil beside his bed. Page 48.

Wallaby selectors last night named the touring squad for the European campaign, which resurrected the rugby union careers of three unlikelys in Tim Wallace, Richard Tombs and Andrew Blades. Surprises included the snubbing of Ewen McKenzie, Tim Gavin and Alistair Murdoch. Page 48.

The Sydney Swans will return to the Victorian Supreme Court today in a bid to have the AFL Tribunal hearing of fullback Andrew Dunkley delayed until after this Saturday's grand final. Dunkley was charged yesterday with striking Essendon forward James Hird. Page 48.
THE AGE

The fairy-tale rise to stardom for the Sydney Swans, which will climax in the AFL grand final this weekend, apparently is still in financial trouble according to confidential documents obtained by The Age, revealing debts of A$2.5 million. Page A1.

Shane Warne has withdrawn from the Tour of India, succumbing to injury. Speculation that a revival of Greg Matthews' cricket career was imminent was dashed with the call-up of Victorian Peter McIntyre, who has only one Test cap of experience. Page B6.

Stan Alves will remain coach of St Kilda for at least another year, with the Saints expected to make an official announcement within the next few days. If the Saints can rise to a top-six position in the AFL, Alves will again be retained for 1998. Page B6.
HERALD SUN

Essendon will seek the maximum compensation of A$150,000 for losing the services of young star, and winner of the 1993 Brownlow medal, Gavin Wanganeen to AFL newcomer Port Adelaide, as Power's first signing in the club's history. Page 86.

A disappointed Kathy Watt has been forced to withdraw from next month's world cycling championship competition because of injury, which has been revealed through ultra sound, as a tear to her hamstring. Page 80.

Melbourne Cup bookmakers have reacted swiftly to the news that jockey Frank Dettori will ride Grey Shot in the event, springing the hopeful in from 50-1 to 25-1. The five year-old has won the Goodwood in England and will start a light 55 kilos. Page 80.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Manly skipper Geoff Toovey will play in Sunday's rugby league grand final against St George with a facial fracture, after tests revealed a fracture to the base of his eye socket, compliments of Cronulla prop Les Davidson last weekend. Page 104.

Wallaby physio Greg Craig has been dumped because of disagreements with other coaching staff, including Greg Smith, stunning players and embarrassing the ARU. Craig is responsible for the rehabilitation of Nick Farr-Jones' and Tim Horan's knee injuries. Page 102.

Manly fullback Matthew Ridge has been ordered to sit a mental speed test before he is declared fit for the weekend's grand final against St George, after being severely concussed in a mis-timed tackle last weekend against Cronulla. Page 98.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
